data.one_liner: Multithreading and worker thread pools for Dart and Flutter using Isolates and Web Workers.
data.what_it_does: Squadron provides persistent worker pools and an abstraction layer to offload CPU-bound and heavy I/O tasks to background threads across platforms (Native Isolates and Web Workers). It handles type safety, task cancellation, streaming return types, and exception marshalling via code generation.
use_when: You need to offload CPU-intensive tasks from the main thread without blocking UI performance.
You need persistent worker pools that stay alive across multiple tasks rather than spawning new isolates repeatedly.
You target both native (Dart VM) and browser platforms with a uniform multithreading API.
avoid_when: Your app only requires simple one-off background tasks where `Isolate.run()` is sufficient and lightweight.
You want to avoid using code generation steps during development.
strengths: Cross-platform support for native Isolates and Web Workers (JS & WASM).
Persistent worker pools for handling frequent tasks efficiently.
Type-safe proxy generation and native Stream support from workers.
weaknesses: Requires manual worker lifecycle management (must call `stop()` to clean up background threads).
data.setup_notes: Add squadron to dependencies and squadron_builder / build_runner to dev_dependencies. Run build_runner to generate workers, and compile workers to JS/WASM for web targets.
